issues.description: The template's state_preparation method for the Lights Out puzzle declares the parameter state_of_lights as type 'str', while the grover_circuit method (in the same template) and the problem statement expect a list[int] representing the board (e.g. [0,0,1,1]). The solution implementation also uses list[int]. This mismatch inside the template will confuse students about the expected input type and may lead to incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature of state_preparation to accept state_of_lights: list[int] (and update its docstring accordingly) so it matches the grover_circuit signature, the problem statement examples, and the solution implementation. This ensures students clearly understand the expected input format.

issues.description: The Quantum Fourier Transform exercises are labeled with different exercise numbers across the problem statement and the code files. The problem statement refers to QFT tasks as Exercise 6 (3-qubit QFT) and Exercise 7 (n-qubit QFT), while the template and solution files use internal comment headings like "Exercise 1.1 / Exercise 1.2" (ex1_qft.py) and "Exercise 2.1 / Exercise 2.2" (ex2_qft.py). This inconsistent numbering for the same conceptual exercises can confuse students when they try to map the problem description to the corresponding template/solution files.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the exercise numbering/labels so the QFT exercises are referenced consistently. For example, update the header comments in ex1_qft.py and ex2_qft.py (both template and solution) to refer to Exercise 6.1/6.2 and Exercise 7.1/7.2 respectively, or adjust the problem_statement.md to match the file-level exercise numbers. Ensure any internal comments and docstrings reflect the same exercise numbers used in the problem statement.
